# Ayush Suryawanshi

> Ayush Suryawanshi is an Indian chemical engineer working across catalysis, electrochemistry and process engineering. Ayush holds an M.Tech in Catalysis Technology from IIT Madras (2026, CGPA 8.51/10), spent a research semester at NTNU, Norway (2025), and has been a Management Trainee at LOXIM Industries Ltd., Ahmedabad, since July 2026. The work spans catalyst synthesis and characterisation, electrode preparation and three-electrode electrochemical testing, DFT and reaction-kinetics modelling, process design and costing, and effluent treatment.

Contact: ayush.suryawanshi0803@gmail.com · LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/in/ayush-suryawanshi

**Education**
- M.Tech, Catalysis Technology, Department of Chemical Engineering, IIT Madras, Chennai, Jun 2024 – May 2026. CGPA 8.51/10. Degree conferred at the 63rd convocation, 17 July 2026.
- Semester exchange, Department of Chemical Engineering, NTNU, Trondheim, Norway, Aug – Dec 2025. UTFORSK mobility scholarship. Thesis catalyst synthesis in the KinCat group, hosted and supervised by Prof. Edd Anders Blekkan.
- B.Tech, Chemical Engineering, Indore Institute of Science and Technology, affiliated to RGPV Bhopal, 2019 – 2023. CGPA 8.17/10, First Division with Honours.
- Senior School Certificate (Class XII, CBSE), Delhi Public School, Chhindwara, 2019. 84.2%.

**Experience**
- Management Trainee, LOXIM Industries Ltd., Ahmedabad (Jul 2026 – present): Led a two-month study on a high-sulphate dye effluent: mapped where the treatment cost goes, compared electrochemical, membrane and crystallisation routes with suppliers, and proposed a treatment train that recovers the waste salt as a product, at about two-thirds lower modelled operating cost. Evaluated electrocoagulation and electroflocculation as pretreatment options. Ran screening, sample trials and feasibility checks with more than ten technology vendors; handed the study over with a validation roadmap for further evaluation. Trained on HPLC, GC-MS, FTIR and UV-Vis; completed plant safety induction and HSE training.
- Deputy Placement and Internship Coordinator, Placement and Internship Cell, IIT Madras (Aug 2024 – Jul 2025): Handled placements and internships for the 2023–25 and 2024–26 M.Tech batches; 75% of M.Tech chemical engineers were placed.

**Skills**
- Electrochemical testing: Autolab potentiostat with NOVA, three-electrode cell, cyclic voltammetry, chronoamperometry, ECSA, one-hour durability holds
- Electrodes and catalysts: Wet-chemical catalyst modification, catalyst ink formulation and Nafion loading, drop-cast electrodes on glassy carbon and carbon paper
- Characterisation: FE-SEM with EDX, powder XRD, BET: reading and interpreting the results
- Computational chemistry: Gaussian 16 (DFT), Avogadro
- Kinetic modelling and process design: Python with Cantera, Aspen HYSYS, Excel, mass and energy balances; capital and running-cost estimates (team project)
- Data analysis: OriginPro
- Handling hazards in the lab: Acids, sodium borohydride, inert-gas (nitrogen and argon) work
- Analytical instruments: HPLC, GC-MS, FTIR and UV-Vis: training
- Plant safety: Plant HSE induction and SOP training
- Technology selection and process economics: Supplier screening, sample trials and feasibility checks; DWSIM simulation and a stage-wise operating-cost model
- XPS: Analysed XPS data in M.Tech coursework
- Courses: M.Tech: Advanced Chemical Engineering Thermodynamics, Chemical Reactor Theory, Transport Phenomena, Experimental Methods in Catalysis, Catalyst Preparation and Characterization Lab, Computational Methods in Catalysis. B.Tech: Material and Energy Balance, Chemical Reaction Engineering, Heat and Mass Transfer, Process Equipment Design, Chemical Process Modeling and Simulation, Process Safety and Hazards Management, Process Plant Economics and Management
- Process simulation: CHEMCAD in B.Tech process simulation labs; DWSIM, self-taught and used in the LOXIM study
- Methods: Linear sweep voltammetry, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, chronopotentiometry, TGA

**Conferences, awards and scholarships**
- Poster on SNCR NOx reduction, Treforedlingsforum 2025, Oslo, Norway (Nov 2025)
- Attended EuropaCat 2025, the European catalysis congress, Trondheim, Norway (2025)
- UTFORSK mobility scholarship, NTNU, for a research semester in Norway (2025)
- GIAN course on characterisation of heterogeneous catalysts, IIT Madras (Apr – May 2025)
- GATE 2024, Chemical Engineering: All India Rank 864, Out of 13,937 candidates (Feb 2024)
- Paper presentation, SCHEMCON 2021, MANIT and IISER Bhopal (Oct 2021)

## Projects
- [Keeping platinum clean in formic acid fuel cells](https://suryawanshi-ayush.github.io/projects/thesis-bi-pt-formic-acid/): Bi-modified Pt/C catalysts and a quinone mediator, tested for how long they hold their current. (May 2025 – May 2026, IIT Madras, with synthesis at NTNU, Norway)
- [A lower-cost treatment train for a high-sulphate effluent](https://suryawanshi-ayush.github.io/projects/loxim-effluent-treatment-study/): A two-month study: where the treatment cost of a dye effluent goes, which routes could replace it, and a proposed train that recovers the waste salt as a product. (2026, two months, LOXIM Industries Ltd., Ahmedabad)
- [Designing an SNCR retrofit for a biomass boiler](https://suryawanshi-ayush.github.io/projects/sncr-biomass-boiler/): A four-person design study: can selective non-catalytic reduction bring a biomass boiler under its NOx limit, and at what cost? (Aug – Nov 2025, NTNU, Trondheim)
- [Reworking a catalyst synthesis after an ignition on the filter](https://suryawanshi-ayush.github.io/projects/ntnu-synthesis-scale-up/): Three batches of Bi-modified Pt/C: a low-yield first batch, an ignition in the second, and a changed aqueous route with no ignition observed. (Aug – Dec 2025, KinCat group, Department of Chemical Engineering, NTNU, Trondheim)
- [Oxygen reduction on a 13-atom platinum cluster](https://suryawanshi-ayush.github.io/projects/dft-orr-pt13/): A DFT study of the intermediates of the four-electron oxygen reduction pathway on Pt13. (Jan – May 2025, IIT Madras)
